Our project is a health-monitoring system designed for astronauts—specifically for use by NASA medical personnel. It consists of a garment equipped with health sensors, worn underneath an astronaut's spacesuit. Should an astronaut's health status reach a critical level—whether by dropping too low or rising too high—NASA doctors will be alerted. The system also includes a manual trigger: a button located in the palm of the astronaut's hand, which can be toggled on or off to prevent false alarms. When the astronaut clenches their fist, a signal—"I AM IN DANGER!"—will be sent to the NASA medical team.
details:
Our project is a smart health monitoring system designed to be integrated into astronauts’ spacesuits. It aims to monitor vital signs such as heart rate, ECG, blood oxygen (SpO₂), body temperature, and breathing rate.

The collected data is displayed on a digital dashboard, helping astronauts and mission teams track health conditions and notice possible changes early.

We developed a dashboard prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Our planned hardware includes health sensors integrated into the spacesuit.

Our project is creative because it combines multiple health-monitoring features into one system. While designing it, we considered astronaut safety, comfort, accuracy, energy efficiency, and reliability.

Our main goal is to support astronaut health and safety during future space missions.
